summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer presented with acute nausea and vomiting, one week after a prior hospitalization for similar symptoms. She had recently received a Botox injection for gastroparesis and noticed dark material in her vomit, likely due to a Mallory-Weiss tear. She was admitted for inability to tolerate oral intake and managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and antiemetics including Zofran, Reglan, and Ativan. A nasogastric tube was placed in the ED but removed by the patient. Her symptoms improved gradually, allowing advancement to a soft diet. Labs showed mild metabolic acidosis and stable hemoglobin, with no evidence of ongoing bleeding. She was discharged home in stable condition on her prior medications with follow-up planned in gastroenterology and primary care.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
